newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Beogradska banka readies for Lon club talks.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Beogradska banka readies for Lon club talks.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Beogradska Banka said on Thursday it will set up a new agency to handle foreign claims and liabilities from its member banks, a move which analysts saw as a preparation for talks with London Club creditors.

The newly appointed general manager of the Beogradska Banka system Borka Vucic said the 20-member banking system will create a commercial agency to first register all commercial debts and claims and then offer them for sale.

"After we have registered all our debts and claims, we shall offer our debt to the market. The debt can be bought through debt-for-equity swaps or creditors may prefer a 25-year rescheduling, but that debt will find its place and will be no obligation of the state," Vucic told Reuters.
Vucic, with a reputation of being a close associate of Serbia's president Slobodan Milosevic, said most of the debt to be taken over by the new agency was to commercial banks.
"In some cases there were credits extended with state guarantees, but most are commercial credits to London club creditors," she said.
Vucic refused to tell the size of Yugoslavia's debt to commercial creditors, but sources close to the government said it ranged between four and five billion dollars.

"Our debt is very small compared to our potential. It is not an exorbitant figure which we cannot repay. It is not our fault that the debt has not been rescheduled. We would have paid it back if there were no sanctions and economic blockade," she said.
Yugoslavia was expecting a portion of its debt to be written off just as the London club practiced in some other cases, Vucic said.
"We would like all our debts to be written off, but seriously, at least that part which carries the highest interest," she said.
In a debt rescheduling deal, Yugoslavia expected a grace period of at least as many years as U.N. sanctions lasted, Vucic said.
